short: The United States formally entered the Second World War in response to the attack on Pearl Harbor.
full:
On 8 December 1941, one day after the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, the United States Congress formally declared war on the Empire of Japan. In an address to a joint session of Congress, President Franklin D. Roosevelt famously condemned 7 December as a date which will live in infamy. The resolution passed almost unanimously, with only a single dissenting vote in the House of Representatives.

The declaration brought the United States directly into the Second World War, ending its official stance of neutrality. Three days later, Germany and Italy declared war on the United States, prompting a reciprocal American declaration. The full industrial and military mobilization of the United States fundamentally shifted the balance of power in favor of the Allies.
